title: Structure sections on a reduced scheme away from component intersections
statement: Let $X$ be a reduced scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$ be closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose underlying sets cover $X$. Put $T=\bigcup_{i\ne j}(Z_i\cap Z_j)$. Then $X\setminus T$ is the scheme-theoretic union of the open subschemes $Z_i\setminus T$, these opens are pairwise disjoint, and for every open $U\subseteq X\setminus T$ restriction is an isomorphism $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)\cong\prod_i\Gamma(U\cap Z_i,\mathcal O_{Z_i})$ (with empty factors omitted).

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NE, proof, first paragraph after setting T

proof.text: For each index a the image of i a is closed by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The finite union T of pairwise intersections is therefore closed. The set W a = T complement intersect range (i a) equals the complement of T union the images with index b different from a: the forward inclusion uses the definition of T, and the reverse inclusion uses the covering hypothesis. Thus W a is open. A point in two distinct W a would lie in T, so the W a are disjoint; their union is T complement by distributivity and the covering hypothesis. All these arguments are implemented directly with finite unions and set membership.

For an open V contained in T complement, set U a = V intersect W a, viewed as an open of X [def-pc-scheme]. Then the U a cover V and the inverse images of U a and V under i a are equal. The restricted closed immersion i a on U a is surjective: each point of U a is in the image of i a. Its target is reduced as an open of the reduced scheme X [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Apply Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_of_isClosedImmersion_of_surjective to obtain an isomorphism. Its map on global sections, transported by arrowResLEAppIso, makes (i a).app (U a) an isomorphism of rings. The equality of the inverse images gives a bijection e a = (i a).appLE (U a) ((i a) inverse image V) from sections on U a to the desired component sections.

Naturality, Scheme.Hom.map_appLE, identifies restriction from V to U a followed by e a with (i a).app V. Injectivity of all e a and TopCat.Sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq' give injectivity of the original map. For surjectivity, choose the unique preimage under each proved bijection e a of the given component section. Equal indices are compatible trivially; distinct U a have empty intersection, whose structure-sheaf sections form a subsingleton. TopCat.Sheaf.existsUnique_gluing' glues the compatible family on the cover of V. The naturality factorization gives the required component sections. Empty opens and an empty index type are included by the same sheaf theorems.

lean.statement: theorem glue_component_reduced_cover_sections {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced X] {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (Z : ι → Scheme.{u}) (i : ∀ a : ι, Z a ⟶ X) [∀ a : ι, IsClosedImmersion (i a)] (hcover : (⋃ a : ι, Set.range (i a)) = Set.univ) : let T : Set X := ⋃ a : ι, ⋃ b : ι, ⋃ (_ : b ≠ a), Set.range (i a) ∩ Set.range (i b) IsClosed T ∧ (∀ a : ι, IsOpen (Tᶜ ∩ Set.range (i a))) ∧ Pairwise (fun a b : ι => Disjoint (Tᶜ ∩ Set.range (i a)) (Tᶜ ∩ Set.range (i b))) ∧ (⋃ a : ι, Tᶜ ∩ Set.range (i a)) = Tᶜ ∧ ∀ V : X.Opens, (V : Set X) ⊆ Tᶜ → Function.Bijective (fun s : Γ(X, V) => fun a : ι => ((i a).app V).hom s : Γ(X, V) → ∀ a : ι, Γ(Z a, (i a) ⁻¹ᵁ V))
